assumptions: Initial state is assumed to be `increase` because the NL lists `increase`, `hold`, and `decrease` in that order and no explicit initial state is given.

`slp` is modeled as an external slip-error input to the supervisor; the wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, and PID computations remain outside this discrete FSM because no equations or PID states were specified.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: single-wheel ABS hydraulic regulator as a three-state FSM
transition guards split the slip-error space; guards use `slp` thresholds

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init: first cycle dispatches the initial transition to increase and applies the increase valve commands.
scenario_results.name: default_init_enters_increase_outputs

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: probes increase -> hold at the inclusive slp <= 0.01 boundary and just above it.
scenario_results.name: increase_to_hold_slp_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: slp exactly 0.01 must trigger increase -> hold and neutralize valves.
scenario_results.name: increase_to_hold_at_threshold

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: probes hold behavior at slp = 0.01 no-fire and slp > 0.01 transition to increase.
scenario_results.name: hold_positive_band_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: slp just above 0.01 must trigger hold -> increase and command pressure increase.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_increase_above_positive_threshold

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: probes hold behavior at slp = -0.01 no-fire and slp < -0.01 transition to decrease.
scenario_results.name: hold_negative_band_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: slp just below -0.01 must trigger hold -> decrease and command pressure release.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_decrease_below_negative_threshold

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: probes decrease -> hold at the inclusive slp >= -0.01 boundary and just below it.
scenario_results.name: decrease_to_hold_negative_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: slp exactly -0.01 must trigger decrease -> hold and neutralize both valves and pump.
scenario_results.name: decrease_to_hold_at_threshold

evidence: NL: "single-wheel ABS hydraulic regulator as a three-state FSM coupled with a PID-based slip controller"
NL: "Wheel speed and vehicle speed are used to compute the slip ratio, and the PID output drives the Stateflow supervisor"
DSL includes only external `slp` plus outputs `k1`, `k2`, `n`; no wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, PID state, PID output, or slip-ratio computation is modeled.
DSL does match the concrete FSM clauses: `increase`, `hold`, `decrease`; entry assignments; and guards `slp <= 0.01`, `slp > 0.01`, `slp < -0.01`, `slp >= -0.01`.
findings.summary: The DSL faithfully captures the three named FSM states, valve/pump entry actions, and all four threshold guards, but it abstracts away the PID/slip-computation coupling described in the NL.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary.metrics.n_states_leaf = 3, matching the required three-state FSM.
inspect_model_to_json_summary.action_count = 3, matching the three state entry actions.
inspect_model_to_json_summary.transition_count = 5, consisting of the initial transition plus the four NL threshold transitions.
GroundingMap source_summary assumes `slp` is an external slip-error input and that wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, and PID computations remain outside the discrete FSM.
findings.summary: Coverage is strong for the discrete hydraulic supervisor component but incomplete for the broader controller context mentioned in the NL.

evidence: NL does not state an initial Stateflow state.
DSL: `[*] -> increase;`
GroundingMap source_summary: "Initial state is assumed to be `increase` because the NL lists `increase`, `hold`, and `decrease` in that order and no explicit initial state is given."
findings.summary: The initial state is not specified by the NL but is fixed in the DSL as `increase`; this is plausible but not textually grounded.

evidence: NL distinguishes the concrete discrete supervisor from continuous wheel-slip dynamics in the plant model.
DSL has variables only `slp`, `k1`, `k2`, and `n`.
No events, PID gains, integrator/derivative states, wheel-speed input, or vehicle-speed input appear in the DSL.
findings.summary: The model is intentionally simplified to the discrete supervisor and does not represent continuous wheel-slip dynamics, wheel/vehicle speed inputs, or PID internals.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary.ok = true with blocking_count = 0 and advisory_count = 8.
Diagnostics include `W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR` for `slp` and `W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE` on each threshold transition.
design_diagnostics_summary.inspect_summary.nl_external_input_vars includes `slp`, reducing the concern from a deterministic error to an advisory structure smell.
findings.summary: Advisory diagnostics are expected for a supervisor with an external input and output-only command variables, but the structure relies on implicit external driving of `slp`.

evidence: warning_budget_exhausted is empty.
design_diagnostics_summary.inspect_summary.warning_budget_state shows repair_count = 0 for all advisory warnings.
The DSL does not add artificial assignments to `slp` to silence `W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR`.
findings.summary: No unjustified warning-driven repair is evident; the model preserves the externally supplied `slp` rather than inventing unsupported internal updates.

evidence: All explicitly listed FSM states, actions, and threshold guards are present.
sim_summary.ok = true with n_scenarios = 9 and n_scenarios_passed = 9.
five_component_summary is empty, so there is no independent FE/NGF/REC/GAS/SCB/AAT/BVS/DMR-style evidence beyond the summaries provided.
The PID/slip-computation coupling is represented only by external variable `slp`.
findings.summary: Estimated NFRR tier: T2 within-scope candidate. The discrete FSM is well covered and executable, but the abstraction of PID/slip computation and the assumed initial state prevent a stronger reviewed-reference tier.

evidence: GroundingMap source_summary explicitly records both assumptions: external `slp` and initial `increase`.
SD-4 diagnostics classified the external-input warnings as advisory rather than blocking.
Simulation scenarios validate the model's stated threshold behavior but do not test PID/slip-computation integration.
findings.summary: The main quality cap traces to SL-1 abstraction choices: it treated the PID output/slip computation as external and inferred an initial state without explicit NL support; later deterministic stages validated syntax and local transition behavior but did not require broader component expansion.
